messages:
kevin (Customer): Hey team — one of our customers is seeing streaming responses from /v1/streams drop mid-response. They get 60-70% of the output, then the SSE connection closes with no final event and no error body. Happens across two regions (us-west2, eu-west1). Happening on our integration for ~5% of sessions since yesterday after an SDK upgrade.

sara (Support): Thanks — can you paste the raw request/response headers (especially the stream X-Request-ID) and a short repro? Also which SDK version?

kevin (Customer): SDK: node-sdk@2.3.1. Repro steps attached by the customer: they open an EventSource to https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams with Authorization header, send a chat payload, then listen to `message` events. They see the final chunk missing sometimes. No 4xx/5xx returned.

ben (SRE): Quick checklist: 1) capture server logs for the X-Request-ID; 2) gather packet capture (tcpdump/tshark) from client side; 3) check proxy/nginx timeouts and buffering; 4) check connection reset counters on LB. Could be intermediate proxy closing the socket early or an incomplete flush from the runtime.

kevin (Customer): They provided one X-Request-ID: req_8c9f21b2. Also included short tcpdump capture but they said it looks normal. They have a private cloud fronting the request (Fastly).

ashok (Eng Runtime): Fastly / Cloudflare often buffer and terminate when they think a connection is idle. For SSE we need continuous keepalives. On the runtime side we send a 1-byte newline keepalive every 15s. If the client and intermediate proxies have different idle timeouts, proxy may close. Can you check the timing of the last server-side write vs the TCP FIN from client?

maria (DevEx): For reproductions, ask them to run this curl command (raw SSE stream) and save stdout to a file so we can diff partial vs complete: 

```bash
curl -i -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b","input":"testing partial streaming reproducible"}' \
  --output - > stream.out
# wait for stream to finish then upload stream.out and `tcpdump -w stream.pcap`
```

sara (Support): Also ask them to capture TLS session IDs and the client side time when they see the last `message` event. If they can get a pcap with TLS keys (exported SSLKEYLOGFILE) that helps us inspect frames in Wireshark.

kevin (Customer): They returned a pcap (uploaded) and the stream.out — I pulled out the HTTP headers. Headers look like: 

```
:method: POST
:path: /v1/streams
:scheme: https
:authority: api.redwood.ai
authorization: Bearer redacted
accept: text/event-stream
content-type: application/json
x-request-id: req_8c9f21b2
```

ben (SRE): Good. I pulled logs for req_8c9f21b2 from the runtime cluster: 

```
[info] req=req_8c9f21b2 start=1765012320.123 node=runtime-5
[info] req=req_8c9f21b2 model=redwood-13b seq_len=512 kvcache=hit state=streaming
[debug] req=req_8c9f21b2 wrote_chunk=2048 bytes at=1765012323.872
[info] req=req_8c9f21b2 stream_closed_by_client=0 server_write_complete=1 close_reason=none
[info] req=req_8c9f21b2 end=1765012324.025 duration_ms=1901
```

ben (SRE): The runtime logged server_write_complete=1 which indicates our process flushed all chunks for the session. That suggests an intermediate network device might have closed the TCP connection after some point and the client didn't re-establish correctly.

ashok (Eng Runtime): Can we see the pcap? If the client TCP FIN comes after our final write, then it's likely client-side or proxy closing. If FIN comes before final write, it's network drop.

kevin (Customer): Uploaded pcap with SSLKEYLOGFILE. Attached packet times show server PSH/ACK with final chunk then FIN from remote ~120ms after last PSH. But the client reported missing final event.

maria (DevEx): Two possible causes: 1) client side EventSource handler dropped the last chunk due to buffering or parsing bug in the polyfill (node-fetch eventsource polyfill notorious for edge-case); 2) intermediate TLS termination (Fastly) reassembled packets differently and some chunks were lost due to connection reuse.

sara (Support): Action items for customer: 1) run curl reproduction with `--raw -vvvv` and upload both stdout and pcap; 2) try disabling any CDN/proxy (direct to our origin) to isolate; 3) upgrade SDK to node-sdk@2.3.2 which has EventSource reconnect heuristics fix.

kevin (Customer): They ran curl --raw: output shows trailing `data: ` line with incomplete JSON in ~2 reproductions. They tried direct origin and still saw one failure out of 30. After upgrading to 2.3.2, they say failure rate dropped to ~0.2%.

ben (SRE): Follow-up checks on our side: check per-node socket resets, kernel OOMs, and nginx proxy buffer logs. I also increased keepalive frequency to 10s for a subset of traffic to see if that reduces failure rate.

ashok (Eng Runtime): Added a temporary tracing span in the streaming pipeline to emit `stream:flush:done` events with packet counters and last-flush timestamp. Also toggled `chunked_flush_min_bytes` to force earlier flushes for small chunks.

observability-bot: New trace created: trace_0a1b2c3d for req_8c9f21b2. View at https://console.redwood.ai/traces/trace_0a1b2c3d

maria (DevEx): If anyone needs a quick repro locally, here's a Node snippet using eventsource-polyfill that reproduces the parse ordering issue when the server sends a bare `\n` keepalive between JSON frames: 

```js
const EventSource = require('eventsource');
const es = new EventSource('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams', {
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.TOKEN}` }
});
es.onmessage = (e) => console.log('MSG', e.data);
es.onerror = (err) => console.error('ES ERR', err);
```

maria (DevEx): Workaround for customers while we finish root-cause: 1) verify SDK >= 2.3.2; 2) enable automatic reconnect with `retry` handling and idempotent resume tokens in SDK; 3) set EventSource polyfill to buffer until terminal `event: done` event.

sara (Support): I'll follow up with the customer summary and ask if they'd like us to open a Priority investigation. They already accepted a support call. Will attach pcap, logs, and trace id.

kevin (Customer): Thanks all — appreciate the quick triage. Will monitor after SDK upgrade and keep you posted. :thumbsup:

ben (SRE): Marking this thread for postmortem if we see recurrence >0.5% across tenants. Also filing infra ticket to tune proxy idle timeouts and keepalive consistency. :+1:

ashok (Eng Runtime): I'll keep the tracing hook enabled for 24h and pull aggregated `stream:flush:done` latencies. If we still see mismatch between server_write_complete and client confirmations, escalate to netinfra.

sara (Support): Closing loop here once customer confirms stable. Thanks team. :heart:
